papers.title: CD19 CAR T cell therapy reshapes the host microbiota immune axis in autoimmune diseases
papers.abstract: CD19 targeted CAR T cell therapy induces profound B cell depletion and clinical responses in autoimmune disease; however, whether it reshapes host microbiota interactions remains unknown. We longitudinally profiled gut microbiome composition and microbiota-specific humoral immunity in 20 patients with systemic lupus erythematosus, systemic sclerosis, or idiopathic inflammatory myopathy undergoing CAR T cell therapy, alongside 23 healthy controls, using shotgun metagenomics, IgA/IgG-bound microbiota profiling, and PhIP Seq. CAR T cell therapy reshaped microbiota directed humoral immunity, with reduced fecal IgA and serum anti commensal IgA and IgG accompanied by selective remodeling of microbiota-reactive antibody repertoires. This finding was paralleled by selective changes in gut microbial composition, including depletion of Bifidobacterium adolescentis, without uniform depletion of disease-associated pathobionts. Integrated host microbiome analyses identified altered predicted protein protein interactions involving the immunoproteasome and B cell plasma cell pathways, with interactions before CAR T cell intervention being significantly associated with subsequent relapse. Consistent with these findings, taxon specific IgA targeting, but not global diversity of IgA IgG coated microbiota, differed according to subsequent relapse. Lower baseline fecal IgA was also associated with delayed B-cell reconstitution, linking mucosal humoral immunity to immune recovery after CAR T cell therapy.

papers.title: Ksp37 is a rapidly mobilized NK cell secretory protein that engages FGF2
papers.abstract: A key feature of natural killer (NK) cells is their preloaded arsenal of effector molecules, allowing them to rapidly respond upon activation. In this study, we characterized a previously unexplored secretory protein, termed killer-specific secretory protein of 37 kDa (Ksp37), which is highly abundant in differentiated CD56dim NK cells. Ksp37 is rapidly secreted in a dose-dependent and JAK-1 dependent manner upon low levels of cytokine stimulation, making it a sensitive readout for NK cell activation. Following secretion, intracellular levels were rapidly replenished, preserving responsiveness to subsequent cytokine stimulation. We found that Ksp37 is stored in polarized intracellular compartments distinct from those containing canonical cytotoxic effector molecules, including granzyme B and perforin, which require stronger stimulation for release. Lastly, we identified Ksp37 as a novel binding partner of fibroblast growth factor 2 (FGF2). This opens new avenues of exploration for the role of NK cells in remodeling their extracellular environment by modulating the FGF2-FGFR1 axis, which plays a key role in tumor growth, angiogenesis and tissue repair.

papers.title: Differential regulation of myeloid Scavenger Receptor A (CD204) expression in humans versus mice in response to sepsis
papers.abstract: Sepsis is the number one cause of mortality in the critically ill patient. The underlying pathophysiology of sepsis is not fully understood. Scavenger Receptor A (SR-A) is a promiscuous receptor of myeloid cells that binds multiple pathogen associated molecular patterns (PAMPs). We have demonstrated that SR-A promotes mortality in murine sepsis. The present study sought to examine the effect of sepsis on myeloid SR-A expression in septic mice and compare it to sepsis patients. Leukocytes were isolated from mice after cecal ligation and puncture. Blood leukocytes were isolated from sepsis patients. Myeloid cells were isolated from healthy mice or human subjects and were treated with PAMPs. Leukocyte phenotype and SR-A expression were determined by flow cytometry. CLP increased SR-A expression when compared to sham operated animals on both neutrophils and monocytes/macrophages. In contrast, SR-A expression was not changed on either neutrophils or monocytes from sepsis patients when compared to healthy control subjects. Treatment of murine neutrophils and macrophages with Pam3CSK4 and treatment of macrophages with LPS increased SR-A expression. Human neutrophil SR-A expression was not altered by any PAMPs, and only treatment with C. albicans glucan increased SR-A expression on human monocytes. Myeloid SR-A expression is increased in septic mice, and this increase plays a detrimental role in the response to sepsis, while SR-A expression is not changed in leukocytes from septic patients and does not correlate with SOFA II scores. Thus, myeloid SR-A expression does not appear to play significant a role in the pathophysiology of human sepsis.

papers.title: HIV broadly neutralizing antibody precursor maturation induced by mRNA vaccination in nonhuman primates
papers.abstract: The induction of broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) is a principal goal of prophylactic HIV vaccines. For many bnAbs, priming ultrarare precursors from the naive B cell repertoire is the first major immunological hurdle. Previous studies have shown that the germline-targeting (GT) priming immunogen N332-GT5 delivered as adjuvanted protein to non-human primates (NHPs) activates bnAb precursor B cells for the human bnAb BG18 targeting the V3-glycan supersite on the HIV envelope (Env) glycoprotein. Here, we engineered N332-GT6 to improve binding affinity to diverse BG18-class precursor naive B cells by 9-fold. mRNA-LNP vaccines expressing N332-GT5 or N332-GT6 as membrane-bound (gp151) trimers were evaluated for their ability to prime BG18-class precursor B cells in NHPs across three related studies. Although N332-GT5 gp151 mRNA-LNP priming induced BG18-class precursor B cells in most animals after two vaccinations, the higher-affinity N332-GT6 gp151 induced responses more consistently after only one immunization. Sequential vaccination with two heterologous mRNA-LNP booster immunizations drove affinity maturation and induced BG18-class memory B cells capable of binding wildtype HIV Env. Together, these findings demonstrate that mRNA immunization can achieve GT priming, boosting, and early maturation of ultrarare bnAb-class B cells in NHPs.

papers.title: Biological aging and comorbidities are linked to HIV 1 reservoir size despite suppressive antiretroviral therapy
papers.abstract: Background The HIV reservoir persists in long-living immune cells after antiretroviral therapy initiation. Proviral DNA integrates at preferential host DNA sites, while HIV transcription continues under treatment, with potential biological consequences. Treated people with HIV remain at increased risk for premature aging and non-AIDS comorbidities compared to people without HIV. Whether HIV reservoir size and activity impact health outcomes during treatment remains unclear. Methods We analyzed 1895 people with HIV using antiretroviral therapy from the 2000HIV cohort to study associations between the reservoir and historic and prospective virologic and immunological response markers, comorbidity outcomes and biological aging scores. The reservoir was assessed by quantifying total and intact proviral HIV DNA in circulating CD4+ T cells, along with measures of HIV transcriptional activity, including cell-associated HIV RNA. Results HIV reservoir markers were highly correlating and associated with older aging scores and adverse virologic outcomes, including quantifiable and residual viremia at study entry and during follow-up. Total HIV DNA, unlike the minor fraction of intact HIV DNA, correlated with prevalent cardiovascular disease, subclinical atherosclerotic disease, liver fibrosis and incident malignancies independent of circulating inflammatory markers and lowest CD4 nadir. Total HIV RNA associated with prevalent cardiovascular disease and liver fibrosis. Conclusion The HIV reservoir associated with older aging scores and long-term health outcomes in people with HIV using antiretroviral therapy, independent of inflammation and immune suppression history. Whether reservoir-reducing interventions lower the risk of non-AIDS comorbidities should be studied in people with high reservoir markers. Funding and trial registration ViiV Healthcare; 2000HIV ClinicalTrials.gov number: NTC03994835

papers.title: Rab27a modulation reverses hemorrhage-induced neutrophil dysfunction in response to secondary respiratory challenge
papers.abstract: Patients recovering from hemorrhage are susceptible to secondary respiratory infections, owing to dysregulated innate immune responses. Using a two-hit mouse model of hemorrhage followed by a secondary respiratory challenge with Staphylococcus aureus or lipopolysaccharide (LPS), we investigated the role of Rab27a in the neutrophil response to pulmonary inflammation and host defense. Hemorrhage followed by S. aureus infection increased surface CD63 expression on pulmonary neutrophils, indicating azurophilic granule release, and was accompanied by reduced neutrophil entry into the airspaces of the lung. Using HoxB8-conditional neutrophil progenitor (NP) transplantation to neutrophil chimeric mice, we observe that Rab27a-deficient neutrophils have enhanced recruitment into the extravascular pulmonary compartment compared with wild-type (WT) neutrophils. Furthermore, pharmacological intervention with Nexinhib20, a small-molecule inhibitor of Rab27a-JFC1 interactions, attenuated systemic and pulmonary inflammatory responses in the two-hit model, including a reduction in circulating myeloperoxidase (MPO) levels. Nexinhib20 also enhanced neutrophil-mediated S. aureus killing that was accompanied by increased intracellular MPO levels in neutrophils. Collectively, these findings implicate Rab27a-associated functions in the regulation of neutrophil trafficking and inflammatory responses following hemorrhage and secondary respiratory challenge, highlighting the potential of pharmacological targeting of Rab27a to attenuate inflammation without compromising antimicrobial host defense.

papers.title: Longitudinal CCR2 PET Imaging Tracks Early Inflammatory Monocyte and Macrophage Infiltration in Experimental Arthritis
papers.abstract: Objective. Recruitment of C-C motif chemokine receptor 2 (CCR2+) inflammatory monocytes and macrophages represent an early event in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) pathogenesis that cannot be tracked noninvasively with existing imaging modalities. We evaluated longitudinal Ga-DOTA-ECL1i positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) to track and quantify CCR2 cell recruitment in experimental inflammatory arthritis. Methods. Longitudinal Ga-DOTA-ECL1i PET/CT imaging was performed in K/BXN serum transfer arthritis (STA) mice. Imaging findings were validated using biodistribution, autoradiography, histopathology, immunofluorescence, microCT, cytokine profiling, clinical assessment, and pain-related behavioral testing. Results. Joint Ga-DOTA-ECL1i uptake increased during the acute arthritis and declined with disease resolution. Increased tracer signal localized to inflamed joints, coinciding with CCR2 monocyte and macrophage infiltration, synovial inflammation, cartilage damage, local CCL2 elevation, and mechanical allodynia. PET uptake correlated with ankle swelling, clinical disease severity, pain, and paw CCL2 levels, with peak tracer signal preceding progressive structural bone remodeling. Conclusion. Longitudinal Ga-DOTA-ECL1i PET/CT enables noninvasive visualization and quantification of early CCR2 monocyte and macrophage recruitment, establishing CCR2 PET imaging as a mechanism-based molecular platform for early detection, risk stratification, and therapeutic monitoring in inflammatory arthritis.

papers.title: Mechanical and chemical macrophage activation differ by arm, not by amplitude
papers.abstract: Mechanical cues are widely reported to polarize macrophages toward an M1-like state, but the claim rests on nuclear factor kappa B/activator protein 1 (NF-{kappa}B/AP-1) effector markers read without a common scale, and the literature does not agree on the sign of the stiffness effect. We asked a quantitative question instead: by what fraction of the chemical M1 response does mechanical perturbation move the interferon-stimulated gene factor 3 (ISGF3)-dependent interferon-stimulated gene module? Scoring ten independent studies of substrate stiffness and applied force against lipopolysaccharide (LPS) + interferon-gamma (IFN-{gamma}) anchors, processed through an identical pipeline, we find a pooled shift of -0.9% of the chemical response (95% confidence interval -6.2% to +4.5%), equivalent to zero at a {+/-}10% margin (p = 0.0019) with a minimum detectable effect of 8.8%. The result is unchanged across three independent ISG definitions. Nor is it a sensitivity failure: the most transcriptionally responsive mechanical contrast rewires thousands of genes while leaving the module inside a size-matched random distribution. Extending to ten further mechanical modalities shows mechanics is not inert toward these genes; shifts run in both directions, but no contrast supported by within-study inference exceeds 15% of the chemical anchor. Rescoring the same contrasts against an NF-{kappa}B effector module anchored on human LPS kinetics separates the two arms: across 21 modality contrasts the effector arm sits 17.7 percentage points above the interferon arm (paired p = 0.032), and in the four designs whose permutation space can reach p < 0.05 the separation is 34 points. Compression moves the effector arm +36% of the LPS anchor (p = 0.002) and the interferon arm -9% (p = 0.004). The separation is absent under static stiffness, where neither arm moves, and its sign is not fixed. A three-arm in-vivo magnetomechanical dataset assigns the effect to the rotating field rather than the internalized particle, raising the effector arm while lowering the interferon arm. Mechanically induced "M1-like" states are not the chemical M1 program rescaled. Where mechanical loading registers at all, it moves the effector arm and not the interferon arm: interferon-stimulated genes are the wrong readout for mechanical perturbation of macrophages.

papers.title: ACE-engineered human iPSC-derived neutrophils enhance host defense against multidrug-resistant bacterial infections
papers.abstract: Severe neutropenia predisposes patients to life-threatening infections, while donor-dependent granulocyte transfusions are limited by availability and variable cell quality. Here, we engineered human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) to constitutively or inducibly express angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) and differentiated them into functional ACE-engineered neutrophils (ACE-iNeu). ACE expression enhanced granulocytic maturation, reactive oxygen species generation, inflammatory cytokine production, and antimicrobial signaling. ACE-iNeu exhibited enhanced bactericidal activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Following adoptive transfer into neutropenic mice, ACE-iNeu significantly reduced circulating and tissue bacterial burdens. Integrated metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses revealed ACE-associated alterations in adenine nucleotide abundance and developmental and inflammatory pathways. Together, these findings establish ACE engineering as a strategy to enhance the production and antimicrobial function of human iPSC-derived neutrophils and support further preclinical development of engineered granulocyte therapies for severe drug-resistant infections.

papers.title: Zebrafish lack canonical necroptosis despite retaining functional RIPK3
papers.abstract: Organismal development, homeostasis and immunity are facilitated by distinct forms of regulated cell death (RCD). These include conserved apoptosis and necroptosis, a proposed backup antimicrobial defence that requires RIPK3-mediated activation of MLKL and is predicted to be absent in several species lacking MLKL. Zebrafish studies have identified a RIPK3-dependent regulated necrosis that is distinct from necroptosis and is pathogenic in tuberculosis. Here, we experimentally confirm the bioinformatics-based prediction that zebrafish lack canonical necroptosis because they lack MLKL, despite retaining functional RIPK3. We take advantage of the finding that Caspase-8 promotes apoptosis while restraining necroptosis; its deficiency is embryonic lethal in mice unless RIPK3 or MLKL is also inhibited. In contrast, we found that Caspase-8-deficient zebrafish are viable through adulthood without obvious morphological defects. Inhibition of related caspases did not compromise viability, arguing against functional redundancy. Finally, Ripk3 overexpression failed to induce death in Caspase-8-deficient embryos. Our work highlights the zebrafish as a model for exploring RIPK3 and extrinsic apoptosis biology in disease contexts in the natural absence of canonical necroptotic execution.

papers.title: The antagonism of sex chromosomes and sex hormones dictates outcomes in Th17 cell-mediated central nervous system autoimmunity.
papers.abstract: Biological sex traits are shaped by the combined effects of both sex hormones and chromosomes. How these factors interact in sex-related autoimmune diseases, such as multiple sclerosis (MS), has been a subject of intense recent interest. Here, using the Four Core Genotype (FCG) mouse model, in which these two variables can be disentangled, we describe an antagonism between sex hormones and chromosomes that potently influences outcomes in T helper 17 (Th17)-driven progressive central nervous system (CNS) autoimmunity. Male gonadal hormones dampen disease severity, irrespective of sex chromosome complement, by promoting a Wnt/{beta}-catenin signaling program associated with a homeostatic, non-pathogenic Th17 phenotype. By contrast, XY chromosomal complement exacerbates Th17 pathogenicity in a recipient sex-dependent manner; we identify the X-linked molecule SUV39H1 as an inhibitor of inflammatory Th17 cell function. Unexpectedly, we found that hormonally and chromosomally female FCG Th17 cells induced far more severe disease than WT female counterparts despite being genetically identical, pointing to a parental imprinting effect in dictating Th17 cell pathogenicity. These latter investigations uncovered Runx2, a transcription factor previously linked to developmental programs, as a novel negative regulator of the pathogenicity of Th17 cells. Together, our findings establish biological sex as a multilayered regulator of Th17 pathogenicity, revealing distinct and sometimes opposing contributions of hormones, chromosomes, and parental inheritance.

papers.title: Tetravalent dengue mRNA vaccination orchestrates balanced four-serotype immunity with durable memory and protection in mice.
papers.abstract: An effective dengue vaccine must establish durable immunity across four dengue virus (DENV) serotypes, evade antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE), and overcome immune imprinting from prior exposure. Here, we developed TetprM-E mRNA-LNP, a tetravalent vaccine comprising LNP-formulated nucleoside-modified mRNAs encoding DENV1-4 precursor membrane-envelope (prM-E) antigens, and evaluated its immunogenicity, durability, protection and breath across serotype-specific immune backgrounds. Three immunization strategies elicited neutralizing titers greater than 1:1500 against each serotype. Passive transfer of immune sera conferred 100% survival and reduced viremia after lethal DENV2 challenge in immunocompromised mice. Vaccination induced DENV envelope (env)-specific CD8+T cells and CD4-dependent germinal-center responses. DENV env-binding antibodies persisted for 34 weeks alongside DENV env-specific memory B cells. Vaccine-elicited sera showed no measurable in vitro ADE. Although monovalent priming initially biased antibody responses, TetprM-E mRNA-LNP vaccination broadened neutralization across DENV1-4 regardless of priming serotype. Together, TetprM-E mRNA-LNP elicits broad, durable, and protective immunity despite serologic constraints from pre-existing immunity.

papers.title: Structural and functional characterization of polyclonal antibody responses reveals shared and distinct antigenic features of RSV and hMPV fusion proteins
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV), members of the Pneumoviridae family, circulate widely and are leading causes of hospitalization for acute respiratory infections in infants and older adults. The viral fusion (F) protein in its prefusion (preF) conformation is the primary target of neutralizing antibodies, yet how naturally elicited circulating polyclonal antibodies are distributed across its antigenic landscape remains poorly understood. Here, we combined serological profiling, site-specific antibody competition assays and electron microscopy-based polyclonal epitope mapping (EMPEM) to characterize preF-directed immunity to RSV and hMPV in healthy adults. All donors exhibited detectable preF-binding antibodies that positively correlated with virus neutralization and broadly recognized multiple antigenic sites, consistent with immunodominance patterns predicted by a surface-centric computational model. Despite this overall similarity, the distribution of responses across individual antigenic sites differed between RSV and hMPV. EMPEM analyses revealed consistent targeting of the highly neutralization-sensitive preF apex (site O) in both viruses, alongside less abundant responses against equatorial and upper-middle epitopes (sites II, III, IV and V). We additionally observed antibody-bound destabilized preF, supporting a model in which antibody binding promotes transient opening of the preF trimer and may interfere with the conformational rearrangements required for membrane fusion. Together, these findings highlight apex-directed antibodies as a prominent feature of naturally acquired pneumovirus immunity in adults and reveal both shared and distinct patterns of antigenic recognition that may inform next-generation vaccine design and antibody-based prophylactics.

papers.title: HCMV glycoprotein B, but not the pentameric complex, is a key target of antibody-mediated phagocytosis
papers.abstract: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) is a leading infectious cause of birth defects globally with devastating fetal health outcomes, and there is currently no HCMV vaccine available. Glycoprotein B (gB) and the pentameric complex (PC) are immunodominant HCMV envelope proteins and candidates of interest in vaccine development due to their ability to elicit strong anti-HCMV neutralization responses. Recent evidence implicates non-neutralizing antibody functions in protection from vertical HCMV transmission, but the involvement of gB and PC in these responses remains incompletely understood. We evaluated immune responses against HCMV elicited by a gB protein subunit vaccine with and without PC in a preclinical rabbit study. Despite improved neutralization and inhibition of cell-associated viral spread, the inclusion of PC did not enhance antibody-mediated phagocytosis or Fc{gamma}R activation against HCMV virions or infected cells compared to gB alone. We additionally found a reduction in phagocytosis function by an HCMV hyperimmune globulin when blocked against gB, but not PC, suggesting that gB is a target of phagocytosis-mediating antibodies while PC is not. Given that antibody-mediated phagocytosis but not neutralization has been associated with protection from vertical HCMV transmission, these findings support the continued assessment of gB, but not PC, as a vaccine antigen for the prevention of vertical transmission via non-neutralizing antibodies to reduce the congenital HCMV burden worldwide.

papers.title: B cells dominate the heart immune infiltrate during chronic infectious cardiomyopathy
papers.abstract: Recent advances in single-cell and spatially resolved multi-omics have revolutionised our understanding of the cellular and molecular niches governing cardiac homeostasis and acute injury. However, the immune-stromal networks sustaining long-term, chronic heart pathology remain poorly defined, largely due to a paucity of physiologically relevant experimental models. Here, through a side-by-side multi-omic comparison of Trypanosoma cruzi-infected mouse models displaying contrasting degrees of chronic myocardial pathology and fibrosis, we define the long-term cellular landscape of the inflamed fibrotic heart. We reveal that class-switched, antibody-secreting plasma B cells represent the predominant immune subset infiltrating the fibrotic myocardium. CellChat intercellular communication modelling identifies plasma cell-fibroblast crosstalk as the strongest immune-stromal interaction in the fibrosis-prone heart, driven by predicted matrix anchoring (CD44-collagen/laminin) and molecular survival axes (App-Cd74, C3-Cr2). Supporting these computational predictions, immunofluorescence and spatial profiling confirm close proximity between plasma B cells and fibroblasts, alongside a striking accumulation of B cells embedded within extracellular matrix-rich cardiac scars. This localised B cell response maintains prominent pools of parasite-reactive and heart-autoreactive antibody-secreting cells despite a lack of detectable parasite signal in their immediate micro-vicinity. Together, these findings identify a matrix-associated plasma B cell-fibroblast niche as a central driver of chronic cardiac remodelling, revealing how persistent tissue scarring can become decoupled from direct local pathogen presence.

papers.title: Cytotoxic CD4+ exTregs expressing KLRG1 retain immunosuppressive function in cancer
papers.abstract: The role of cytotoxic CD4+ T cells in cancer remains controversial, with both pro- and anti-tumor functionality described. Based on a prior observation that putatively cytotoxic KLRG1+ FoxP3- conventional T cells (Tconv) associated with tumor progression, we deeply investigated the phenotype and function of KLRG1+ Tconv in multiple murine tumor models and in human clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) specimens. We found KLRG1+ Tconv have a conserved, highly activated, terminally differentiated phenotype across species. In murine tumors, KLRG1+ Tconv resemble tumor-infiltrating regulatory T cells (Tregs) at both transcriptional and proteomic levels, upregulating a spectrum of exhaustion-related checkpoint receptors, producing IL-10 and granzyme B (GzmB), and silencing expression of IFN{gamma} and TNF. Functionally, KLRG1+ Tconv exhibited immunosuppressive function in ex vivo assays. Using an in vivo Treg fate mapping approach in tumor-bearing mice, we found a subset of KLRG1+ Tconv are derived from Tregs that have lost FoxP3 protein expression. Ex vivo functional assays demonstrated the exTreg component of the KLRG1+ Tconv compartment is responsible for IL-10 production and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine expression. In treatment studies, we found that KLRG1-targeted antibody-mediated depletion was more efficient than anti-KLRG1 blockade at slowing tumor growth and improving survival, with responses associating with depletion of intratumoral KLRG1+ Tconv and Tregs. In sum, our study discovered a novel conserved pathway of CD4+ T cell plasticity, wherein intratumoral, cytotoxic KLRG1+ CD4+ Tconv cells can be derived from Tregs and maintain immunosuppressive function, despite loss of FoxP3, and that KLRG1-targeted depletion may outperform KLRG1 blockade as an immunotherapeutic strategy in cancer.

papers.title: Dual CD40/CD28 co-stimulation reprograms the solid-tumor microenvironment to unleash CAR-T and endogenous anti-tumor immunity
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has shown limited efficacy against solid tumors, owing to poor T-cell persistence, an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) and cancer immune evasion. Here we describe LACO-Stim (lymphocytes-APC co-stimulator), a chimeric co-stimulatory molecule composed of an agonistic anti-CD40 single-chain variable fragment (scFv) and the CD28 intracellular signaling domain, such that a single molecule activates CD40-expressing antigen-presenting cells while delivering CD28 co-stimulation to the T cell that bears it. Co-expressed with a 4-1BB-based CAR (LACO-CAR-T), it enhanced anti-tumor activity in vitro and achieved durable, complete in most mice, tumor regression rather than transient control in xenograft and immunocompetent models. In immunocompetent hosts, LACO-CAR-T activated dendritic cells, reprogrammed tumor macrophages toward M1-like, antigen-presenting states, and induced epitope spreading with endogenous CD8 T-cell responses against tumor neoantigens. Single-cell transcriptomics and RNA-velocity analysis revealed coordinated immune remodeling: T cells shifted toward a more stem-like, less terminally exhausted state, regulatory T cells declined in frequency and suppressive function, and myeloid cells acquired antigen-presentation programs while excessive inflammatory and suppressive signaling was restrained. LACO-Stim further synergized with anti-PD-1 blockade to control tumor growth. LACO-Stim thus enables CAR-T cells to coordinate intrinsic T-cell reinforcement with extrinsic immune reprogramming, converting an immunosuppressive TME into a de-inflamed (reduced inflammatory signaling), de-suppressed rather than merely armed niche that supports endogenous anti-tumor immunity.

papers.title: IL13 critically contributes to the antitumor activity of polyfunctional CD4+ T cells driven by constitutively active Stat5
papers.abstract: The presence of polyfunctional T cells capable of concurrently producing multiple cytokines correlates with favorable clinical outcomes in patients with cancer. We previously reported that overexpression of constitutively active Stat5a (CASTAT5) confers polyfunctionality on tumor-specific CD4 T cells, enabling durable antitumor immunity following adoptive cell therapy. However, the mechanisms underlying the enhanced antitumor effects of CASTAT5-modified T cells remain unclear. Here, we identify interleukin-13 (IL13) as a critical effector cytokine contributing to the multifaceted antitumor activity of CASTAT5-conditioned polyfunctional CD4 T cells (C5-CD4). C5-CD4 T cells exhibit a prominent T helper 2 (Th2) cytokine profile, accompanied by extensive epigenomic remodeling at the Th2 cytokine loci, as revealed by Hi-C and histone-modification CUT&Tag assays. Neutralization of IL13 diminished the antitumor efficacy of C5-CD4 T cells. Furthermore, targeted Il13 disruption substantially impaired tumor control and was associated with reduced donor T cell expansion and persistence, diminished systemic cytokine and chemokine responses, and attenuated activation of endogenous tumor-reactive CD8 T cells. Nonetheless, IL13 overexpression alone in donor CD4 T cells failed to fully recapitulate the therapeutic activity of C5-CD4 T cells, indicating that IL13 is a critical contributor but is insufficient to account for the full antitumor activity conferred by CASTAT5. Single-cell RNA sequencing associated donor-derived IL13 with increased representation of tumor-infiltrating myeloid cells and IL13-signaling in monocytes and macrophages exhibiting tissue-repair-associated transcriptional programs. Moreover, Il13 disruption diminished the therapeutic efficacy of CASTAT5-expressing CD19-targeted CAR-T cells in a mouse B-cell lymphoma model. Reanalysis of a human CD19CAR-T infusion-product dataset further revealed an association between IL13 expression and type 2 cytokine signatures linked to prolonged clinical response, suggesting a potential contribution of IL13 to the efficacy of human CD19CAR-T therapy. Together, these findings uncover an unexpected antitumor role for IL13 and establish it as a critical node linking polyfunctional donor T cells with endogenous immune cells to promote sustained tumor immunity.

papers.title: Identification and localization of bone marrow ILC2s using Id2/Cxcr6 dual-reporter mice
papers.abstract: Type 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s) are present in the bone marrow, where their identification and spatial localization remain challenging because of their low abundance and the expression of shared markers by other lymphoid populations. Here, we evaluated the use of Id2YFP/+ Cxcr6GFP/+ dual-reporter mice to identify and visualize bone marrow ILC2s. Using spectral flow cytometry, we showed that both ST2- and ST2 ILC2s expressed high levels of ID2, whereas CXCR6 expression differed between these subsets. However, the ID2 expressing compartments also contained NK cells, NKT cells, conventional T cells and ILC progenitors. Surface marker profiling identified CD25 and ICOS as useful markers for enriching ILC2 populations, with ST2 enabling the segregation of the ST2- and ST2 subsets. Single-cell RNA sequencing further characterized the diversity of Id2 and Cxcr6 expressing lymphoid populations and supported the use of CD5 and NKp46 as exclusion markers. Combining these markers with the dual-reporter system, confocal microscopy revealed YFPGFPCD5-NKp46- cells compatible with an ILC2 phenotype, distributed throughout the bone marrow as isolated cells or within multicellular clusters. Complementary flow cytometric analyses demonstrated that ILC2s accounted for more than 90% of a phenotypically related reporter-positive population after exclusion of major T and NK cell populations, providing additional support for the identification of the cells visualized in situ as putative ILC2s. Together, these findings establish a strategy combining dual-reporter mice, flow cytometry, transcriptomic profiling and confocal imaging to investigate the localization and spatial organization of putative bone marrow ILC2s.

papers.title: Deep CyTOF immune profiles of ex vivo granulomatous responses to Mycobacterium tuberculosis differ with European and African geographical origin
papers.abstract: Genetic and environmental factors influence human immunity and modulate responses to infection. Accounting for immune heterogeneity across human populations is critical to the design of novel vaccines and host-directed interventions that would optimally benefit populations experiencing the highest disease burden. Tuberculosis (TB) burden is unevenly distributed across geographical regions and our understanding of the differential immune response to Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) across human populations remains limited. Here, we sought to evaluate the impact of geographical origin on ex vivo granulomatous responses to Mtbinfection. We found that peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from healthy African donors exhibited greater control of Mtbgrowth ex vivo than those isolated from European individuals. High-dimensional single-cell profiling of the granulomatous responses by cytometry by time-of-flight (CyTOF) revealed divergent profiles based on the specimens' geographical origin. Monocytes from European donors displayed a pro-inflammatory phenotype - correlating with Mtbgrowth -, whereas PBMCs of African individuals were enriched in activated, cytotoxic T cells - correlating with Mtbcontrol. Reduced inflammatory response in African monocytes following various microbial stimulations was confirmed. Taken together, our comprehensive immune profiling indicates that environmental and genetic factors shape a cytotoxic-regulatory response that promotes bacterial control. Against the current "one-treatment-fits-all" approach, our findings support the use of specimens from intervention-relevant settings to inform the targeted design of TB vaccines and host-directed interventions.

papers.title: Systemic TLR7 agonism moderates disease severity in acute DSS-induced colitis in mice
papers.abstract: Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7) is an endosomal sensor of single-stranded RNA, studied for its antiviral and pro-inflammatory functions. Its role in intestinal inflammation is undefined, and no approved or clinical-stage therapy for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) engages this pathway. Here we report that systemic administration of the reference TLR7 agonist GS-9620 (vesatolimod) moderates disease severity in acute dextran sodium sulfate (DSS)-induced colitis in mice. GS-9620-treated mice lost less weight, had lower Disease Activity Index scores, and were protected from DSS-induced colon shortening. Immunophenotyping of the spleen showed reduced Th17 and Tr17 populations and an increased proportion of regulatory T cells. These findings indicate that pharmacological TLR7 agonism is not merely tolerated in the inflamed intestine but is associated with a shift of the systemic immune compartment toward a regulatory phenotype. The results identify TLR7 as a candidate disease-moderating target in IBD and motivate direct tests of causality, route and chronic-disease relevance.

papers.title: Deep phenomics of African green monkey and Baboon PBMCs using a 30-marker spectral flow cytometry panel
papers.abstract: Vaccines are the best way to prevent and combat diseases. Non-human primate (NHP) models have proven to be the gold standard model for studying the efficacy of certain vaccine candidates prior to human trials. Cell-mediated immunity serves as a surrogate marker for predicting vaccine efficacy. Despite the availability of deep-immunophenotyping panels for T cells in the peripheral blood of humans, their application to NHPs, particularly African Green Monkeys (AGMs) and baboons, remains limited. Notably, AGMs are valuable for HIV and COVID-19 research, while baboons are utilized for pertussis research as a natural infection model and vaccine trial. To overcome such limitation, using spectral flow cytometry, we developed a 30-parameter panel to profile major immune cell subsets (B cells, NK cells, DCs, monocytes) either in AGM or baboon PBMCs. We also profiled T cells, memory phenotypes, functional cytokines by tracking established Th1 markers IFN{gamma}, TNF and IL-2; Th2 markers IL-4/5/13 and the Th17 marker, IL-17, activation-induced markers (AIMs) and FoxP3+ Tregs in both AGM and baboon PBMCs in steady state as well as in mitogen stimulated conditions. For AIMs, CD69, CD134 (OX40) and CD137 (4-1BB) are included and validated in both NHP species. This panel holds potential for exploratory analysis of the impact of these functional cytokines, AIMs, or Tregs on host immunity following infection or vaccination. The panels high level of customization empowers researchers to tailor it to their specific research needs.

papers.title: Cholinergic modulation engages a CHRM1-IL-17 neuroimmune axis to promote diabetic wound repair
papers.abstract: Chronic non-healing wounds are a major complication of diabetes, where persistent inflammation fails to transition into effective tissue repair (1-3). Here we identify cholinergic modulation as a mechanism that promotes productive inflammation and diabetic wound healing. Using a healing-associated fibroblast signature derived from single-cell profiling of human diabetic foot ulcers (3), we identified the acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitor metrifonate as a candidate inducer of reparative wound programs. Topical delivery accelerated healing in diabetic mice and increased acetylcholine availability within the wound. Complementary receptor pharmacology identified muscarinic acetylcholine receptor 1 (CHRM1) as the principal receptor mediating the reparative response. Transcriptomic and cellular analyses revealed early induction of IL-17-associated inflammatory programs and enrichment of CHRM1NK1.1 innate lymphocytes. Depletion of NK1.1 cells or neutralization of IL-17A abolished the pro-healing effect, whereas spatial transcriptomics revealed treatment-associated organization of NK cells within vascular niches. Localized treatment further promoted repair in diabetic porcine wounds and human skin models. Together, these findings identify a CHRM1-IL-17 neuroimmune axis linking cholinergic modulation to diabetic wound repair and establish local AChE inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy for chronic wounds.

papers.title: Impaired Fermentation in the Absence of Gut Microbiota Promotes Inulin-Induced Intestinal Inflammation
papers.abstract: Background and aims: Inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD) are characterized by altered gut microbiota composition and impaired dietary fiber fermentation, which can complicate symptom management. Although inulin is a well-established prebiotic fiber, it can exacerbate gut inflammation under certain conditions. We hypothesized that impaired microbial fermentation leaves intact inulin in the gut to activate epithelial immune receptors and promote inflammation, whereas effective fermentation reduces this pro-inflammatory signaling. Methods: We used germ-free (GF) and conventional (CONV) interleukin-10 knockout (Il10-/-) and wild-type (WT) C57BL/6J mice to assess the role of microbial fermentation and host genetic susceptibility in IBD. GF Il10-/- mice were colonized with fecal microbiota from ulcerative colitis (UC) patients or healthy individuals with fiber intolerance (FI). Mice were fed inulin or structurally distinct, physicochemically matched fiber analogs. Colonic inflammatory and barrier-related gene expression and protein levels were assessed by qPCR and ELISA. Results: In GF Il10-/- mice, inulin, but not cellulose, induced weight loss, diarrhea, and rectal prolapse. Increased colonic toll-like receptor expression (TLR2, TLR4) as well as elevated serum amyloid A (SAA) and lipocalin-2 levels indicated immune activation by unfermented inulin in GF mice. Colonization with dysbiotic microbiota attenuated these effects. {beta}-fructan fibers including fructooligosaccharides and chicory-derived inulin elicited marked inflammatory responses, whereas agave-derived inulin did not, highlighting the influence of fiber composition in inflammation associated with IBD. Conclusions: Effective microbial fermentation is essential for host tolerance to fermentable fibers. These findings underscore the need of personalized nutrition when recommending fiber supplementation in immune-compromised individuals or those with gut dysbiosis.

papers.title: The Src family kinases Lck and Fyn promote transendothelial migration of T cells
papers.abstract: The ability of T cells to cross endothelial barriers and migrate into and within peripheral tissue is crucial for adaptive immunity. Integrins such as LFA-1 play an essential role in this process by acting as adhesion molecules and initiating signaling events that drive the cytoskeletal changes needed for cell migration, however, many of the specific signaling events that promote T cell migration are still unknown. Here, we found that the Src family kinases Lck and Fyn are needed for efficient T cell migration. Primary T cells lacking Lck, Fyn, or both kinases exhibited defects in random migration on ICAM-1 coated surfaces for parameters such as speed and mean squared displacement. Analysis of signaling revealed that Lck was required for PI3K signaling downstream of LFA-1, while Fyn was not. Mechanistically, we found that the absence of Lck disrupted the normal interaction of the PI3K regulatory subunit p85 with tyrosine-phosphorylated binding partners, suggesting that Lck may regulate PI3K activity by controlling p85 protein-protein interactions. Importantly, both Lck and Fyn were required for efficient T cell transmigration across an inflamed endothelial barrier, a critical event for tissue infiltration. Lastly, a small-molecule Lck kinase inhibitor also decreased PI3K signaling and T cell transmigration, indicating the kinase activity of Lck is needed. Together, these data identify a new role for Lck and Fyn in promoting T cell transmigration.

papers.title: IL4Ra Controls The Medullary Dwell Time Of Mature Thymocytes By Scheduling Their Release From The Thymus
papers.abstract: Following their generation, newly produced single positive (SP) thymocytes must remain in the thymus to undergo post-selection maturation, a process supported by the thymic medulla. This ensures that SP thymocytes are equipped with functional competence prior to S1PR1-mediated thymic emigration. Despite this importance, the intrathymic mechanisms that control the balance between retention and release of SP thymocytes is unclear. Here, we describe a cell autonomous requirement for IL4Ra-signalling in SP thymocytes, that determines the duration of their medullary occupancy. We show that the period of this occupancy is prolonged in the absence of IL4R expression by SP thymocytes, which occurs as a result of impaired interactions with medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTEC). Importantly, extending the duration of medullary occupancy enhances the maturational status and functional capabilities of SP thymocytes, including improved TNF and IL2 production. Collectively, we show that IL4Ra regulates the medullary occupancy of mature thymocytes, which in turn determines the functional properties of thymic output.

papers.title: TMEM11-Dependent Cristae Architecture Restrains Imiquimod-Induced NLRP3 Inflammasome Activation via Mitochondrial ROS
papers.abstract: Imiquimod (IMQ) is a clinically approved drug widely used to treat skin malignancies; however, its application frequently provokes severe inflammation through NLRP3 inflammasome activation. The mechanism underlying IMQ-induced activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome is not completely defined. While IMQ-induced inhibition of mitochondrial electron transport chain complex I is necessary for activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, it is not sufficient; suggesting presence of additional targets/triggers. The role of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) as the additional trigger to activate the inflammasome remains contentious based on conflicting reports. Using a unique genetic model lacking expression of mitochondrial membrane protein TMEM11 we reaffirm the role of mtROS in IMQ-induced NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Macrophages deficient in Tmem11, a mitochondrial contact site and cristae organizing system (MICOS)-associated membrane-protein, exhibit ultrastructural defects in cristae morphology without altering mitochondrial mass or mtDNA copy number. Loss of TMEM11 influences cristae length and density, reducing mitochondrial oxygen consumption. Tmem11-deficient macrophages exhibit normal NLRP3 inflammasome activation in response to canonical agonists (e.g., ATP, nigericin) but show caspase-1 hyperactivation and exaggerated IL-1{beta} and IL-18 secretion upon IMQ treatment. This exaggerated response is rescued by antioxidant treatment, confirming the role for mtROS. These findings demonstrate that cristae architecture restrains drug-induced mtROS to limit NLRP3 activation and that mtROS is a primary driver of IMQ-mediated NLRP3 inflammasome activation.

papers.title: Structural evolution of Fcα/μR-mediated antibody recognition
papers.abstract: The Fc alpha-mu receptor (Fc/R) is an ancient Fc-receptor sharing common ancestry with the polymeric Ig receptor (pIgR) and binding polymeric IgM and IgA ligands. In several vertebrate lineages, including birds, Fc/R may serve as the sole IgM and IgA Fc receptor; yet its evolution and ligand-recognition mechanisms across vertebrates remain poorly understood. Here, we identify FCAMR expression in duck (Anas platyrhynchos, ap) lymphoid tissues and demonstrate that recombinantly expressed apFc/R ectodomain binds apIgM and apIgA ligands. apFc/R affinity was ~10-fold higher for apIgM versus apIgA and ~10-fold higher than mouse (mm) Fc/R. Cryo-EM structures of apFc/R in complex with pentameric apIgM (3.27 [A]) and tetrameric apIgA (3.57 [A]) showed three Ig-like domains (D1-D3) bound asymmetrically with 1:1 stoichiometry. Comparisons to avian pIgR, which contains four Ig-like domains (D1-D4), revealed overlapping contacts between apFc/R-D1 and pIgR-D1. apFc/R D2-D3 engaged sites similar to pIgR D3-D4, yet formed distinct contact networks. Parallel analysis of a mmFc/R-mmIgM structure (4.13 [A]) revealed mmFc/R's single Ig-domain bound analogous to apFc/R-D1 and to mammalian pIgR-D1, whereas downstream ectodomain regions were not observed. Collectively, the data elucidate PIGR-family mechanisms across vertebrates, providing a foundation for delineating common and divergent functions.

papers.title: Circulating CD4 regulatory T cells are broadly preserved in Parkinson's disease despite altered HELIOS expression
papers.abstract: Background Regulatory T cells (Tregs) are an important component of adaptive immune regulation and have been implicated in Parkinson's disease (PD), with previous studies suggesting altered Treg proportions, phenotype and, in some cases, function. However, existing studies have been limited by variable phenotyping approaches and a lack of detailed functional assessment. Given the growing interest in Tregs as potential therapies in PD, better understanding of their phenotype and function in the disease is important. Methods Circulating FOXP3+ Tregs were characterised in individuals with PD and age-matched healthy controls (HC) using a 24-colour spectral flow cytometry panel. Treg suppressive function was assessed by their ability to inhibit proliferation and cytokine production by polyclonally stimulated autologous T effector cells in vitro. Treg lineage stability was assessed by analysis of FOXP3 TSDR demethylation. Results The proportions and phenotypic characteristics of circulating CD4 Tregs were broadly similar between individuals with PD and HCs, as were Treg suppressive function and FOXP3 TSDR demethylation. However, naive CD4 Tregs from individuals with PD showed reduced HELIOS expression, with a similar but non-significant trend in FOXP3 expression. Reduced HELIOS expression was also observed in the CD8 naive Treg compartment. Conclusions Major quantitative or functional abnormalities in circulating Tregs do not appear to be a dominant feature PD. However, reduced HELIOS expression in naive Tregs suggests more subtle phenotypic alterations that warrant further investigation. The broadly preserved suppressive function is reassuring for therapeutic approaches aimed at increasing Treg numbers, although it will be important to establish that expanded Tregs retain a stable phenotype and suppressive function in inflammatory and tissue environments.

papers.title: Photomechanical engineering of immunogenic whole-cell vaccines by laser-induced vapor nanobubbles for bladder cancer prophylaxis
papers.abstract: Whole-cell cancer vaccines can provide broad tumor-antigen repertoires, but their efficacy depends on manufacturing methods that inactivate tumor cells while preserving immunogenic danger signals. Here we show that laser-induced vapor nanobubbles (VNB) generated from dextran-coated iron oxide nanoparticles provide a drug-free photomechanical route to engineer immunogenic whole-cell vaccines against bladder cancer. Using MB49 murine urothelial carcinoma cells, we established VNB conditions that induced rapid tumor-cell killing together with calreticulin exposure and extracellular ATP and HMGB1 release. Rapid cell killing and calreticulin exposure were also reproduced in the molecularly distinct UPPL1541 bladder cancer model, supporting the generalizability of the early photomechanical response across bladder cancer cell lines. Vaccination with VNB-killed MB49 cells reduced tumor incidence and growth after subcutaneous challenge and enhanced splenocyte-mediated antitumor activity against MB49 cells. In an orthotopic bladder cancer model, vaccination prevented MRI-detectable tumor formation and was associated with marked early bladder enrichment of CD8 T cells and inflammatory monocytes. A single administration of the VNB-generated vaccine preparation showed no evident local or systemic toxicity during seven days of follow-up. These findings provide proof of concept for an externally triggered, drug-free manufacturing approach in which short laser irradiation induces rapid photomechanical killing of tumor cells on demand, generating immunogenic whole-tumor-cell vaccine preparations for further evaluation in therapeutic, post-resection and tumor-derived settings.
